:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.6`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/usePackageJsonEngines`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**warning**](/reference/diagnostics#warning).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`package-json/require-engines`](https://eslint-plugin-package-json.dev/rules/require-properties/require-engines)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"usePackageJsonEngines": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Require the `engines` field in `package.json`.

The `engines` field lists the versions of Node.js and other tools that a package works
with. Package managers such as npm read this field and warn when someone installs the
package with a version outside that range. Without the field, nobody gets that warning,
and the package can fail in ways that are hard to connect to an unsupported version.

The rule only checks that the field exists at the top level of the file. It does not check
what the field contains. It applies to every `package.json` file, including packages that
set `"private": true`.

## Examples

### Invalid

```json title='package.json'
{
    "name": "my-package",
    "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

### Valid

```json title='package.json'
{
    "name": "my-package",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "engines": {
        "node": ">=20"
    }
}
```
